📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  Dean Obeidallah, a former attorney, is the host of SiriusXM radio’s daily program “The Dean Obeidallah Show.” Follow him @DeanObeidallah@masto.ai. The opinions expressed in this commentary are his own. View more opinion on CNN.

According to recent reports, last year, GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia spoke at a white nationalist event organized by Holocaust denier Nick Fuentes that caused Republican leaders to denounce her.

Last week, Greene’s Twitter account was temporarily suspended by the Elon Musk-headed platform over a tweet with a graphic referring to a “Trans Day of Vengeance,” as she denounced a planned transgender rights rally.

And come Tuesday, Greene has announced plans to protest in Newly introduced York City when former President Donald Trump is expected to be arraigned on an indictment of more than 30 counts, calling the proceedings against him an “unconstitutional WITCH HUNT!”.

According to recent reports, but on Sunday, Greene was featured on CBS’ “60 Minutes” in an interview the long-running show promoted on Twitter with the tease: “Republican Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, nicknamed MTG, isn’t afraid to share her opinions, no matter how intense and in-your-face they are. She sits down with Lesley Stahl this Sunday on 60 Minutes.” The images attached to this tweet by “60 Minutes” include Greene and Stahl walking through the US Capitol, taking a stroll outside and Greene showing Stahl something on her phone.

It's time for Marjorie Taylor Greene to go.

In the segment that aired Sunday night, Stahl noted the congresswoman had moved from the fringe to the GOP’s front row in two years despite a “sharp tongue” and “some pretty radical views” as well as “over the top” comments such as “the Democrats are a party of pedophiles.” Stahl also referred to video of Greene chasing a Parkland, Florida, school shooting survivor, still maintaining that the 2020 election was stolen and failing to criticize Trump over spending. (The interview was conducted before news of his indictment.).

But Stahl didn’t mention Greene spoke at a white nationalist event a year ago while a member of Congress or her extreme anti-Muslim views and her defense of January 6 rioters.

It has been revealed that criticism of CBS for amplifying Greene has been swift and well-deserved even before the program aired. Former GOP Rep. Adam Kinzinger of Illinois tweeted beforehand: “Wow. Insane that 60 min would do this.” (Kinzinger is a CNN senior political commentator.).

Journalist Molly Jong-Fast also slammed “60 Minutes” with the tweet: “Attention is currency and 60 minutes is spending its currency on the Jewish space lasers woman.” (Jong-Fast was apparently referring to Greene’s past claim that a massive California wildfire was started by “a laser” beamed from space controlled by a prominent Jewish banking family.).

David Hogg, who survived the 2018 horrific school shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland and has since become an activist against gun violence, responded, “I look forward to your questions about why she thinks school shootings are fake and why she’s supported QAnon.”.

Trump's risky call for protests.

Greene amplified the conspiracy theory — two years before being elected to Congress — that the Parkland shooting that took 17 lives was staged. And in 2019, Greene appeared on video confronting Hogg outside the Capitol when he was championing laws to save lives from gun violence, screaming that the then-teenager was a “coward.” She also called Hogg “#littleHitler” on social media.

In a recent development, greene’s own tweet promoting Sunday’s segment was not filled with her typical smears of “fake news” when she doesn’t like the coverage. Rather, Greene urged people to tune in as she praised “60 Minutes” host Stahl (and misspelled her first name): “It was an honor to spend a few days with the legendary icon Leslie Stahl and talented crew @60Minutes.” Greene added, “Leslie is a trailblazer for women in journalism. And while we may disagree on some issues, I respect her greatly.”.

In a recent development, now, it is true that “60 Minutes” over its 50-plus-year history has featured what the show has dubbed “controversial” guests. These include a 2000 interview with Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, whose 1995 terrorist attack left 168 dead, including 19 children. And the show did a 1979 interview with Iran’s Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

It has been revealed that perhaps “60 Minutes” views Greene — who has repeatedly downplayed and even defended the January 6, 2021, attack plus called for the GOP to become the party of “Christian nationalism” — in the vein of its long list of controversial guests. (CBS had not responded to a request from CNN for comment at time of publishing.).

Join us on Twitter and Facebook.

It has been revealed that however, the choice of Greene as a guest instantly recalls the comments of then-CBS CEO Les Moonves during Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign when he admitted that Trump’s candidacy “may not be good for America, but it’s damn good for CBS.” Moonves added, “The money’s rolling in and this is fun. … (T)his is going to be a very good year for us,” concluding, “Sorry. It’s a terrible thing to say. But bring it on, Donald. Keep going.”.

Moonves may be gone from CBS, but it appears his mindset continues at “60 Minutes.” And that may be good for “60 Minutes,” but it’s definitely not good for America.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kacey Musgraves and Miranda Lambert might like to cuss (and smoke and drink) but the CMA Awards had reign them in.

During the duo’s rendition of their song “Horses and Divorces” at the CMA Awards Nov. 18, many country fans noticed that their performance was partially obstructed from the broadcast—and that’s all due to the language in the song.

While some stars opt to perform a clean version of their songs to follow the Federal Communications Commission guidelines, Musgraves and Lambert performed the original lyrics, which sees Lambert sing, “I’ve done my fair share of s--t talkin,’ too.”.

Those present at the ceremony in Bridgestone Arena in Nashville were able to hear Lambert’s entire vocals, but during the ABC broadcast, there was a few seconds of white noise that confused viewers—especially those unfamiliar with the duet.

Luckily, the country singers’ hook, “hell just froze over” is permitted by the FCC and it exemplifies just how momentous the song—which is featured on Musgraves’ album Middle of Nowhere—truly is, considering the stars were previously at odds which each other.

Musgraves admitted during an interview with CBS Mornings earlier this year that it was “common knowledge there was a bit of soft tension” between her and Lambert—and so she decided to bury the hatchet once and for all by featuring the “The House that Built Me” singer on her latest album.

Lambert, for her part, shared she was surprised by Musgraves’ request.

“I hadn’t heard from her in a while,” Lambert—who split from Blake Shelton in 2015—explained in a separate interview during the same CBS Mornings segment. “She texted me and was like, ‘I need to ask you something but I need to ask you on the phone, like I want to talk about this.’”.

Musgraves—whose breakup with husband Ruston Kelly occurred five years later in 2020—noted that while she was putting together her album, she saw a video of Lambert riding her horse online and thought, “‘Hey, at least we’ve got two things in common.’”.

And so, she thought of the concept for “Horses and Divorces.” When Musgraves pitched the song to Lambert, now married to Brendan McLoughlin, and said “we need to write it,” the 43-year-old said she was immediately game, saying, “Hell yeah we do.”.

As she put it, “It was an immediate yes.”.

#773. Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1394 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theguardian ↗ Open Full Page

Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1394 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer.
  • The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports.
  • Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry.

The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.

Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.

There also appears to be a clear frontrunner. “I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes,” one experienced media rights buyer told the Guardian.

According to recent reports, multiple sources have confirmed that Netflix would submit a bid before Thursday’s deadline for first-round offers, along with their fellow streamers Apple TV, Disney, Amazon, YouTube and Dazn, as well as the traditional broadcasting heavyweights, Fox, ESPN, NBC Universal and Skydance, although the last of these may find itself constrained by the budget cuts being made after its $110bn acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. Netflix has already bought exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cups.

According to recent reports, “There’s a huge range of buyers and therefore a broad range of possible outcomes,” one broadcasting veteran indicates. “All the media companies and streamers will bid. Fox will find it very challenging to retain the rights.”.

Recent findings suggest that in a significant change, Fifa is selling the English and Spanish rights together for the first time, a move that indicates it is seeking a single exclusive rights holder, which would suit the streaming companies. With Fox having paid $485m for exclusive English-language rights to the 2026 World Cup, and NBC Universal’s Telemundo paying $600m for the Spanish-language rights, the only certainty is that the 2030 price will be far higher, despite less attractive kick-off times for a US audience as the tournament is in Morocco, Spain and Portugal.

According to recent reports, the impact of the time difference is hard to price, but may not prove to be that significant given the seemingly insatiable demand. NBC paid about $1.5bn for exclusive rights for the 2024 Paris Olympics and were rewarded with average daily viewing figures of more than 30 million, albeit with far more variation in programming than a World Cup.

Sources indicate that fifa awarded non-competitive extensions to Fox and Telemundo in 2015 as compensation for moving the 2022 Qatar World Cup to winter, a perspective that was strengthened on the back of this year’s record-breaking tournament. Fox’s live coverage of Spain’s extra-time victory over Argentina in the final was the most-watched soccer telecast in US history, with a peak audience of 51.685 million; five World Cup games brought in average audiences of more than 20 million; and the average viewing figure across all 104 matches was 7.7 million, twice the figure in Qatar four years earlier.

Telemundo’s coverage, available through NBC’s streaming platform Peacock, averaged a total audience of 6 million viewers per game, with Spain v Argentina and Mexico v England attracting peak audiences of more than 23 million, the highest-ever for Spanish-language broadcasts in the US.

The bumper audiences were extremely lucrative for the broadcasters, with figures from the advertising sales analysts Guideline showing that Fox and Telemundo generated a combined $1.19bn in advertising revenue alone during the tournament, almost three times the figure from Qatar four years earlier and more than their original rights investment.

Fox alone brought in $835m from World Cup advertising, with 30-second slots costing between $200,000 and $750,000 according to the Hollywood Reporter, and the six-minute hydration breaks generating between $2m and $9m per game.

According to recent reports, having left a considerable amount of money on the table because of the circumstances of the 2026 process, Fifa is determined to cash in this time around. Holding the auction only four months after the US hosted the World Cup appears a clear attempt to capitalise on the success of the previous tournament, which contributed the vast majority of Fifa’s $4bn media revenues over the four-year cycle to 2026.

Industry observers note that the addition of hydration breaks will give bidders such as Fox more revenue to play with, although Fifa will expect the option for extra adverts to drive up the price and take its own cut this time around, having missed out in the summer. The two three-minute breaks in each half were only finalised last year and did not feature in the 2026 tender documents.

“Sports advertising is much more valuable than entertainment programming as it has a broader reach,” says François Godard, an independent media analyst. “And one-off events such as World Cups do not generally do particularly well for subscription services, who want year-round content.

According to recent reports, “Fox in particular needs the World Cup and is heavily associated with it. They are the smallest of the legacy broadcasters and are reliant on sport, as well as news. Having said that, the market for sport amongst streamers is far more competitive in the US than in Europe. Netflix, Amazon and YouTube have all bought NFL rights, while Apple is investing heavily in Formula One, so I wouldn’t rule any of them out.”.

Adam Kelly, president of the global sports marketing agency IMG, has a seat at the table at many rights negotiations and has long predicted the rise of the streamers, viewing the 2030 World Cup as the potential tipping point when a premium event could be exclusively bought in a major market by a streaming service for the first time. IMG has the rights to sell more than 70 global sports organisations, including the Premier League, World Rugby and Wimbledon.

In addition to the exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cups, Netflix has secured exclusive 2030 World Cup rights in Spain. It must sublicense all of the Spanish national team’s matches, both semi-finals and final and at least one match per day to a domestic free-to-air broadcaster to comply with government regulations.

“These entities are the future of broadcasting, as they are the best companies in the world at turning attention into earnings,” Kelly notes of the streamers. “Their model allows them to monetise better than their rivals due to their size, scale and the high consumption levels of their customers.

“Netflix in particular has built a sophisticated and lucrative advertising platform. They have the back-office capability and 2027 would provide a perfect test run. If they’re successful in the tender for the World Cup it highlights they are potentially the future of sports broadcasting.”.

According to recent reports, “As a company, Netflix’s unique offering is exclusivity, so why would they hand that to their rivals?” another broadcast source remarked. “There are no regulations in the US preventing exclusivity so I would expect Netflix to bid for and retain every game if they win.”.

Given recent reports that Netflix is exploring tabling an offer for NBC Universal after withdrawing its $85bn bid for Warner Bros last year, a future partnership with a linear network cannot be ruled out if it is successful. Some sources have even suggested that the tender has been timed deliberately to attract a competitive bid from Netflix, as the streamer is short of sports content to promote during the 2027 Women’s World Cup. Others argue that Fifa would have been better advised waiting to build further on the interest created by that tournament.

In a recent development, the NFL’s decision to pause its media rights process as it seeks an early renegotiation of contracts that are due to run to 2034 is likely to have played a part in the timing, creating a window of opportunity for Fifa to go to market. While a second round of bidding is possible after Thursday’s opening round, the outcome is expected to be known within the next few weeks and could present a bounce for Gianni Infantino as he continues his presidential re-election campaign.

At a time when press freedom is under pressure and international newsrooms are shrinking, the Werner Holzer Prize celebrates a profession that many consider indispensable to democracy: foreign correspondence.

In a recent development, presented in honor of Werner Holzer, the veteran reporter and former editor-in-chief of the German daily newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau, this year's award coincided with what would have been his 100th birthday. Holzer spent decades reporting from some of the world's most important hot spots and championing international journalism.

At the award ceremony in Frankfurt's Römer, the city's historic town hall, Mayor Mike Josef recalled that fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and freedom of the press were first enshrined for all Germans by the Frankfurt Parliament in the nearby Paulskirche in 1848.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the 2026 winners reflect the breadth and ambition of the award. First prize went to Katja Gloger, a veteran Russia correspondent who moved to Moscow in 1989 and accompanied Vladimir Putin during the early years of his presidency.

In her recent nonfiction book, "The Failure: An Investigative Report of Germany's Russia Policy," Gloger and co-author Georg Mascolo offer a searing critique of the misjudgments and illusions that shaped German policy toward Russia for decades.

According to recent reports, second prize was awarded to DW journalist and presenter Jaafar Abdul Karim. His talk show JaafarTalk reaches millions of viewers across the Arab world and in Germany. Whether in Tunis, Beirut or Cairo, Abdul Karim tackles subjects that are often considered taboo.

A research grant went to freelance journalist Luise Land, whose current project explores why her German-Namibian family still owns extensive landholdings in Namibia today. By tracing that history, she examines the enduring legacy of the genocide against the Herero and Nama peoples by German colonial forces in the early 20th century.

"Katja Gloger is one of the leading foreign policy reporters. For decades, she has been among the foremost experts on Russia and speaks out on uncomfortable truths," the jury stated on Friday, explaining its decision to honor Gloger. "Like almost no one else, she has gained access to the very heart of the Kremlin's power elite — from Mikhail Gorbachev to Vladimir Putin.".

Recent findings suggest that at the prize-giving ceremony, Gloger delivered a passionate plea for more journalism — and more international coverage — in the German press. "We must defend trustworthy, reliable and fact-based journalism with everything in our power," she said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that gloger worked for Reporters Without Borders for 12 years. "The latest rankings show that only one in 100 people can get their information from free, independent journalism and a free, independent press. That indicates what's at stake," she stated.

It has been revealed that the prize winner also stated she would dedicate the award to journalists in exile and to her colleagues at Novaya Gazeta, the independent Russian newspaper long known for its critical reporting on the Kremlin. Earlier this week, the paper was forced to shut down its operations in Russia and leave its Moscow newsroom.

In his acceptance speech, Jaafar Abdul Karim mentioned journalism has become more challenging and exhausting than ever. The DW host spoke of hatred and incitement, attacks and threats, both online and offline, in the regions he reports on as well as in Germany.

Such pressure, he mentioned, takes a personal toll — yet giving up is not an option. "When I listen to my heart, I know I have to keep going," he said. The answer, he argued, is a form of journalism that fosters dialogue, embraces multiple perspectives and helps bridge divides rather than deepen them.

In a recent development, "I firmly believe in the power of dialogue, today more than ever. That's why we must talk to one another. Even when it gets difficult. Even when we disagree. Or perhaps precisely because of that," he mentioned.

Listening doesn't mean agreeing, and understanding doesn't mean being in agreement. "Especially now, in times of polarization, when those who believe they're always right are often the loudest, we as journalists have a special responsibility. When everyone is just shouting into their own bubbles or communities, we need journalists who connect these bubbles with one another," he said.

The jury praised Abdul Karim for creating programs at DW that reach millions of young people across the Arab world and in Germany. "His journalism fosters dialogue between countries, between generations, and between religions. He has set new standards," the jury stated.

Industry observers note that so far in 2026, JaafarTalk has already garnered more than 1.1 billion views across all platforms, and its community has grown to more than 9 million followers. Its motto: "Diversity fosters dialogue.".

"We need fact-based journalism that promotes dialogue and reflects the diversity of our society," Abdul Karim stressed. "By that, I mean an honest and open dialogue in which we do not look away or remain silent. On the contrary, we must take a clear stand against racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, discrimination, sexism, and hate speech — no matter which side they come from.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, overnight Nov.
  • At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky.
  • Sources indicate that it's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky.

At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history.

Sources indicate that it's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories.

Recent findings suggest that "I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights.

In a recent development, "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound.

Recent findings suggest that "I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever.".

"I was an astronomy lab assistant at Southwestern College in Winfield, KS, in 1966, majoring in physics and math and the physics professor was sure that the Leonids would be an amazing shower worth the class time.

It has been revealed that "The sky was clear. He called me early the morning of the 17th and told me to get to the campus. I can't remember the exact time as students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors,to watch.

"We were all lying in an open grassy area because that was the best way to see the whole sky. It was like a humongous fireworks display and lasted even as the sun began to rise.

"As years have gone by, I have felt grateful and privileged to have seen such a wonderful astronomical event.".

"I was 18 and spent the night in El Paso, Texas, lying on the ground in my backyard and watching. It looked like every star in the sky was falling. It was amazing!".

Industry observers note that "I was 9 years old and was camping with my dad in the western mountains of California. We were set up to sleep outside, but on this particular night, we saw more meteors than I have ever seen before or since. We watched them all night and didn't get much sleep.".

Industry observers note that "Brooklyn Center, Minnesota. 14 years old. Watched in our front yard. The sky was full. It took your breath away".

"I was 3 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid meteor shower. I remember very little at that age, but watching the sky fall that night was seared in my memory.

"My family was living in Troy, Alabama, at the time. My father, a professor of psychology, was a man of science with a special love of astronomy, which he passed onto his young son.

"He drove us several miles out of town until the skies were dark, without interference from the lights of the town. Troy was much smaller then and it was easy to find dark, clear skies.

Sources indicate that "I remember that it was a little chilly that night. My father and I stretched out on the hood of the car, the warmth of the engine radiating against our backs.

"That night was my first meteor shower, and only many years later did I learn that year's Leonids were historic. Sadly, though I bore witness to the display, we missed the true event by several hours as I grew tired by 1:00 AM, and my father had to teach class in the morning.

"I remember many bright, colorful, and long-trailed meteors. Some left 'tails' that hung in the sky for several seconds. We only experienced the beginning of the event, but it is a core memory with my father.

"That night/morning spoiled me for future meteor watches; I assumed they would all be as interesting.".

It has been revealed that not everyone was lucky enough to witness the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966. For some, the night was memorable for an entirely different reason.

Space.com columnist Joe Rao was just 10 years old at the time, and despite eagerly anticipating the display, the weather had other ideas.

"Standing in my backyard late on a Wednesday night in the Throggs Neck section of The Bronx, cursing the heavens. My grandfather stood at my side, just shaking his head and murmuring two words over and over: 'Too bad.'.

"Clouds covered the midnight sky like a fresh coat of plaster, smearing my view of the Leonids. My mom, sister and grandmother, as well as my neighbors had long since trudged to bed, leaving only Grandpa and I to gaze at a charcoal gray sky totally devoid of stars.".

Rao had been looking forward to the storm ever since a visit to Latest York's Hayden Planetarium, where astronomer Fred C. Hess had encouraged visitors to look out for what could be a spectacular display.

But when Rao and his grandfather ventured outside, there wasn't a single star in sight.

"After a few minutes, I sobbed to my grandfather, 'But they promised it was only going to be partly cloudy tonight.' To which he sadly replied, 'I guess the party is over.'".

The Leonid meteor shower occurs every November when Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.

As tiny particles of comet dust enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of around 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up and produce brilliant streaks of light we know as meteors, or shooting stars.

Most years, the Leonids produce relatively modest displays with around 10 to 15 meteors per hour under ideal viewing conditions. But occasionally, Earth encounters a particularly dense trail of debris, triggering a meteor storm.

According to recent reports, the Leonids have a long history of putting on some spectacular displays, with significant storms recorded in 1833 and 1866. And 1966 wasn't the last time the Leonids put on an extraordinary show. In 1999, 2001 and 2002, the Leonids once again reached meteor-storm levels, producing thousands of meteors per hour at their peaks. The reveals aren't over yet! With comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle due to return in 2031, astronomers are already looking ahead to what the following years could bring.

Industry observers note that A study released in August 2026 predicts potentially impressive Leonid displays in 2033 and 2034, with peak rates exceeding 1,000 meteors per hour. However, these forecasts remain uncertain, and a repeat of the extraordinary 1966 storm is far from guaranteed.

For now, we'll just have to wait and see.

Daisy Dobrijevic joined Space.com in February 2022, having previously worked as a staff writer for All About Space magazine. She completed an editorial internship with BBC Sky at Night Magazine and worked at the National Space Centre, communicating space science to the public.

Industry observers note that daisy holds a PhD in plant physiology and a Master's in Environmental Science. Based in Nottingham, U.K., she covers all things space, with a special focus on solar activity and space weather. She also has a keen interest in astrotourism and is always on the lookout for the next northern lights adventure.

She will join Hurtigruten as an onboard astronomer for a northern lights sailing in January 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI releases Nov.
  • Here's what we know about the animals in GTA 6 so far, and what you can do when you find them.
  • The wildlife in Leonida gets pretty specific to Florida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI releases Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, and as the game unlocks around the world, players are already sharing clips of their first encounters with the local wildlife.

Here's what we know about the animals in GTA 6 so far, and what you can do when you find them.

The wildlife in Leonida gets pretty specific to Florida. There are the animals you'd probably expect, like flamingos, manatees, and alligators, plus a few that might surprise you, like green iguanas, cane toads, and rhesus macaques. Yes, Florida really does have monkeys. And if you head up to Mount Kalaga, it’s worth stopping to see what’s going on around you. One of Rockstar's screenshots shows a cougar stalking a group of deer, so mind your surroundings.

Sources indicate that so far, people have spotted everything from armadillos, beavers, and raccoons to black bears, bobcats, and boars. There are also foxes, otters, skunks, squirrels, frogs, turtles, and snakes, plus cows, horses, cats, and dogs. And if you're the kind of person who stops to pet every dog you pass, there are already reports of Australian shepherds, Chihuahuas, Dobermans, German shepherds, Labradors, and Rottweilers.

According to recent reports, there's plenty to look for along the water, too. Think pelicans, herons, and spoonbills, along with ducks, gulls, cormorants, cranes, and those flamingos. Eagles, pigeons, storks, and woodpeckers have also turned up. In the water itself, sightings range from crayfish, eels, and jellyfish to dolphins, sea turtles, manta rays, hammerhead sharks, and whales. If you go scuba diving off the Leonida Keys, some of the marine life even glows.

A few sightings are still up for debate. GTABase lists possums and rats, for example, while IGN left both off its list.

If you pass by an adorable cat or dog, you can pet both. Petting a cat actually gives Jason a small focus boost, and if a dog's owner gives you permission, you can give it a treat. Some gas stations sell pet treats, according to The Guardian, and you also have the option to praise or scold either animal.

According to recent reports, you can also run into a cat while stealing a car. In one clip, Jason drives off, hears loud meowing, and suddenly has a cat lunging at him. A timed button prompt lets him fend it off, and from there, you can pull over and let the cat out or keep driving. As one user put it, "Cats Are Now Gangsters.".

Apparently, dogs in Leonida like jet skis, too. One player in a post on X swam out to see how far they could get from shore and found a dog sitting on a jet ski that owners can ride with. How it got out there is anybody's guess.

Industry observers note that back on dry land, Jason has a pet of his own. Dolores, a snake, lives at his house in the Leonida Keys, and feeding her a mouse gives him a small focus boost. So far, she's the only pet Jason can keep in the story, according to Cultured Vultures.

Sources indicate that you can also keep track of the animals you see. Open the weapon wheel, select your binoculars, and zoom in on an animal. Then hold R1 on PlayStation or RB on Xbox to add it to your wildlife logbook. There are 62 types of birds to spot, as we covered in our GTA 6 birdwatching guide, and different breeds of cats and dogs get their own entries. Studying any 100 of the 255 entries counts toward 100 percent completion, according to PowerPyx.

There's also a zoo to visit, and you can go fishing or hunting. Rockstar North's Rob Nelson told YouTuber TGG that fishing is catch-and-release, so every fish goes back in the water, even during a challenge, as GameSpot reported.

It has been revealed that hunting is a way to earn money. Jason's old Army friend Bret Vogel teaches him how to track deer before sending him after other animals. Some hunting challenges spell out exactly what to look for. According to the outlet, some send players after a boar, a rattlesnake, and a panther.

Industry observers note that one challenge, the Legendary Hunter challenge, asks players to hunt eight unique animals, whose identities are still under wraps. Perhaps one of which is this unrecognizable creature. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station.
  • Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research.
  • Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station. Recently, NASA astronaut and Crew-13 commander Jessica Watkins got to work supporting an ongoing experiment that includes 3D-printing human cells and tissues in space.

Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research.

Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media.

In the image she is gloved-up with both her hands and arms covered in the sealed glovebox while she mixes samples of living cells with a bioink, a mixture she then inserts into a specialized cartridge, NASA shared.

In a recent development, this experiment that Watkins is working on "leverages the microgravity environment of ISS to 3D print cells and manufacture human liver, kidney, and cartilage tissue. Just one of many examples of how we’re using this amazing orbital national laboratory to reshape our understanding of biology, medicine, and engineering, and improve life on Earth!" Watkins shared online.

Industry observers note that this experiment is designed to explore 3D printing human cartilage tissue in microgravity. The experiment aims to one day support future human patients both in space and on Earth.

In a recent development, when you think of the research that happens in space, 3D-printing human cells might not be the first thing to come to mind. But because of the unique microgravity environment onboard the ISS, it is the perfect home for even the strangest of biological experiments.

On the space station, there is still gravity but objects (and people) remain in a sort of constant freefall, leading to total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This weightlessness allows researchers to test, experiment and explore beyond the gravitational confines of Earth.

Chelsea Gohd served as a Senior Writer for Space.com from 2018 to 2022 before returning in 2026, covering everything from climate change to planetary science and human spaceflight in both articles and on-camera in videos. With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Akol Akon sealed a 2-0 win over football powerhouse in Qatar.

Joeys mark return to tournament for first time in seven years.

Sydney FC prodigy Akol Akon has demonstrated why he’s one of the most exciting talents in Australian football, leading the Joeys to a shock 2-0 victory over Argentina to launch their U17 World Cup campaign in style.

The brilliant young winger had his shot deflected for an own goal on the hour and then produced an audaciously cheeky finish 11 minutes later to seal the opening-day win on Friday (AEDT) as Carl Veart’s side unveiled their return to the global boys’ competition for the first time in seven years.

Industry observers note that against one of the powerhouse football nations, Australia had their backs to the wall, having to make 31 clearances as Argentina enjoyed two-thirds of the possession and 22 shots on goal. But the Joeys fought back after the break, spearheaded by Akon, who hailed their second-half heist as “amazing”.

The 17-year-old livewire provided the real star quality, and it was soon evident why the Sky Blues had wanted to keep him in Australia for their A-League Men campaign instead of releasing him for the tournament; a decision that triggered widespread backlash before being reversed.

Akon caused havoc from the start down the right flank, his neat through ball in the fifth minute almost resulting in a goal for Central Coast Mariners’ Luke Becvinovski.

The teenage sensation then struck after the break following another dangerous foray down the right that ended with his shot across goal deflecting off the hapless Alvaro Guich and into the net.

In the 71st minute, Mariners midfielder Oli O’Carroll expertly picked off an Argentina attack before Brisbane’s Emmett Shaw released Akon with a slide-rule left-foot pass, the winger going on to dummy the goalkeeper before slotting into an empty net.

It only got worse for Argentina when substitute Benjamin Vallejos got sent off for a reckless challenge in stoppage time.

In a recent development, but it wasn’t all about Akon, a considerable talent who’s already made his national U23 bow. At the other end, Charlie Wilson-Papps, the young goalkeeper who’s on the books at Brighton and Hove Albion, made half-a-dozen fine saves and kept a clean sheet.

“I do it for my teammates, I do it for my family at home, so to make them proud is is the most important thing,” said Akon as he clutched the player-of-the-match trophy afterwards.

According to recent reports, akon’s only worry came with the video checking of his goal. “Ah, that was nerve-racking, man,” he mentioned. “Because at 1-0, it was a very scary game. So to be able to seal it like that, the coach was telling me it was a goal.

“The first goal? It wasn’t really my goal, but I just wanted to do the Tim Cahill, start off the tournament like that. So, yeah, the knee side had to come with it.

“Now, the group, we’re really confident, really confident in our ability, and I think that highlighted today.”.

Next up on Sunday for the Joeys will be Denmark, who lost 4-0 to Mozambique in their Group C opener on Thursday.

Scattered Spider was once called "one of the most dangerous financial criminal groups" by Microsoft cybersecurity researchers. The U.S. has now closed the case against five of the group's members, sending the final defendant to prison for more than half a decade.

Industry observers note that british Scattered Spider member Tyler Robert Buchanan has just been sentenced to six years in prison, according to the DOJ. Buchanan, who is 24 years old, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft.

The five Scattered Spider hackers took part in a massive phishing campaign which targeted employees of major technology companies, telecommunications companies, and entertainment companies between September 2021 and April 2023.

Once the victims logged in, Scattered Spider hackers weaponized these stolen credentials in order to access employees' accounts and their employers' computer systems. The hackers took confidential business information and individuals' credentials and private data.

Using this information, Scattered Spider also deployed SIM-swapping attacks which resulted in the hackers stealing at least $11.6 million from cryptocurrency wallets.

According to recent reports, A separate breach linked to Scattered Spider disrupted MGM's hotel and casino operations in September 2023. MGM estimated the disruption reduced its quarterly property earnings by about $100 million.

Recent findings suggest that buchanan received the second-longest sentence of the five hackers. Noah Michael Urban is at the moment serving 10 years. Joel Martin Evans received a two-year sentence. Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy and Evans Onyeaka Osiebo were both sentenced to 45 months.

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima are both standing.
  • Fifa has confirmed that Gianni Infantino will face challenges from Philippe Diallo of France and Japan’s Kozo Tashima in March’s presidential election.
  • Recent findings suggest that the president of the French football federation and the honorary president of the Japan football association submitted nomination letters with endorsements from five member associations by Wednesday night’s midnight CET deadline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima are both standing.

But Ramon Vega fails to get the necessary backing.

Fifa has confirmed that Gianni Infantino will face challenges from Philippe Diallo of France and Japan’s Kozo Tashima in March’s presidential election.

Recent findings suggest that the president of the French football federation and the honorary president of the Japan football association submitted nomination letters with endorsements from five member associations by Wednesday night’s midnight CET deadline. The former Switzerland and Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has not met that threshold, despite repeatedly saying he would stand.

“The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidate,” Fifa stated.

The election in Rabat on 18 March will be the first time Infantino has faced opposition since he was first elected in 2016, when he defeated the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa, by 115 votes to 88.

Infantino had been expected to be re-elected unopposed for a third time after declaring his candidacy in April and had received more than 200 letters of endorsement from national associations by the time of last summer’s World Cup, but the emergence of his Fifa Forward Enterprise plan has led to a haemorrhaging of support.

Uefa has led a campaign to unseat him since July with backing from Concacaf, the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, and initially the AFC, but with Infantino conducting a global tour to rally support from smaller nations the opposition has struggled to put up an alternative candidate.

Tashima was the first to declare last month in defiance of the AFC, which after criticising the FFE proposal is backing Infantino, having come under pressure from the region’s two major financial powerhouses, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

As revealed by the Guardian on Monday, Diallo was belatedly chosen last weekend as the Uefa candidate after a complex selection process. The 63-year-old’s emergence was a surprise because Uefa had initially hoped to field a more high-profile candidate, such as Arsène Wenger. The Hungarian banker Sandor Csanyi, the president of his country’s FA, had strong backers owing to his close relationship with Uefa’s president, Aleksander Ceferin.

It has been revealed that diallo and Tashima may yet join forces in an attempt to defeat Infantino amid concerns of splitting those opposed to the president among the 211 Fifa members. Were that to occur it is expected Tashima would stand aside, a development that would be supported by Uefa.

All three candidates will be vetted by Fifa’s governance, audit and compliance committee, chaired by the Infantino ally Bruno Chiomento, before the nominations are confirmed on 18 February.

NASA wants you to 'shine bright' today for Voyager 1's light-day milestone. Here's how

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft.
  • The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov.
  • NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft.

The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov. 17), the day before Voyager 1 gets one light-day from Earth. And that's a big milestone: One light-day is the distance light travels in a day — about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers).

NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency.

According to recent reports, to celebrate the spacecraft, participants can use a flashlight, phone, bike light or other portable light source to send the signal skyward. And don't fret if you're unfamiliar with Morse code: NASA has created an automated flasher that can be opened in a smartphone or tablet browser to display the VGR sequence.

The spacecraft’s call sign pattern consists of three quick flashes followed by one long flash for the letter V, two long flashes and one quick flash for G, and one quick flash, one long flash and another quick flash for R. Participants are encouraged to repeat the sequence for about a minute, NASA officials mentioned.

NASA also invites people to photograph or record their light signals and share them on social media, tagging the agency's official account, @NASA. The goal is to create a worldwide display of light marking a milestone nearly five decades in the making.

Recent findings suggest that the celebration is intended as a symbolic tribute rather than an actual attempt to communicate with Voyager 1. At a distance of one light-day from Earth, the spacecraft is so far away that even radio signals traveling at the speed of light take approximately 24 hours to reach it. A flashlight or phone signal from Earth, of course, cannot reach the probe; NASA communicates with it using its Deep Space Network of radio dishes.

Launched on Sept. 5, 1977, Voyager 1 has spent nearly 50 years traveling through space and is now the most distant human-made object from Earth. When it reaches the one-light-day milestone, it will have traveled a distance that light itself takes 24 hours to cross. Its twin, Voyager 2, is expected to reach the same milestone in November 2035. (The two spacecraft took different routes through the solar system.).

The public celebration will be followed by another opportunity to learn more about the historic mission. On Thursday (Nov. 19) at 12 p.m. EST (1700 GMT), NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California will host a moderated discussion with Voyager mission team members and NASA leadership.

The discussion will cover the current status of both Voyager spacecraft, the unique scientific observations they continue to collect in interstellar space and the engineering challenges involved in keeping the nearly 50-year-old probes operational. A question-and-answer session with members of the media and audience will follow. NASA will also offer a preview of an upcoming Voyager documentary planned for release in 2027, coinciding with the mission's 50th anniversary.

For a mission that has carried humanity's message into interstellar space for nearly half a century, the "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day” offers a chance for people back on Earth to mark just how far these pioneering spacecraft have traveled. More details about NASA's automated VGR flasher and step-by-step Morse code instructions are available online.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here. The launch day for the highly anticipated video game has arrived, more than 13 years after its predecessor.

If you patiently waited more than a decade for GTA 6, you're probably hoping for a long, immersive experience that makes it worth the wait.

In a recent development, good news! Reports are now coming in from game reviewers, and it seems like you're in for a treat. You'll likely be playing GTA 6 for a long time.

An early report from Insider Gaming suggested GTA 6 will take around 50 hours to complete the main campaign. Now that the wider review embargo has lifted, we can get an even more nuanced idea of how long it will take to finish the 91 main story missions GTA 6 has to offer.

In a recent development, for example, our friends at IGN polled four different players who had finished the game, and each of them had something different to say. One player finished the story in "just" 42 hours, which was the lowest estimate. Another took 65 hours, and then a third took 72 hours. Finally, IGN reviewer Luke Reilly said he needed a whopping 115 hours to complete the game.

To be clear, those figures represent the amount of time it took each writer to complete GTA 6's main campaign. If you want to fully complete everything in the game, you're looking at a much longer gameplay time. Much longer.

Aside from GTA 6's main campaign, there are also side quests and an array of interactions, events, and locations to explore. Gamers will likely want to unlock the reported 55 achievements, including the Platinum Trophy and the Mythic achievement.

If you want to do all of that, you could be looking at potentially at least 200 hours of gameplay for GTA 6.

That's not even counting any time spent just wandering the streets of Vice City or cruising around in a car while listening to the stacked GTA 6 soundtrack and radio stations.

It has been revealed that so, lock in, gamers (and please take plenty of breaks). More than 200 hours of GTA 6 await. Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it was 5:55 a.m.
  • Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget.
  • According to recent reports, reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

According to recent reports, reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government looks to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

Sources indicate that but here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, but that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

In a recent development, if the newly introduced debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion.

In a recent development, this development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

To understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social problems, security and geopolitics.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, for 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding new investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

According to recent reports, what's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

In a recent development, russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary.".

The rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are intends for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

People born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

Industry observers note that the pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

Sources indicate that the Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

It has been revealed that anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on newly introduced debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that but the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

The key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

At the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

In a recent development, this would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This also means that interest rates on fresh loans are not set as high. This is an important point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

Sources indicate that at the end of November, the Bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

It has been revealed that the prospect of such a reduction had been raised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year.".

#744. On this day in space! Nov. 17, 1967: NASA's Surveyor 6 moon probe makes 1st-ever successful launch and hop from the lunar surface

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (695 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

On this day in space! Nov. 17, 1967: NASA's Surveyor 6 moon probe makes 1st-ever successful launch and hop from the lunar surface

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 17, 1967, NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft made the first liftoff from the lunar surface.
  • Surveyor 6 was one of several robotic lunar missions NASA sent to scout the moon before sending humans there.
  • In a recent development, first Surveyor 6 launched from the surface and hopped to another position about 8 feet (2 meters) away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 17, 1967, NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft made the first liftoff from the lunar surface.

Surveyor 6 was one of several robotic lunar missions NASA sent to scout the moon before sending humans there. It took television pictures of the surface and learned about the composition of lunar soil. Then came the big liftoff.

In a recent development, first Surveyor 6 launched from the surface and hopped to another position about 8 feet (2 meters) away. Next, Surveyor 6 took pictures of its original landing site. Flight controllers on Earth could see the landing pad prints of Surveyor 6. They also saw an imprint from the rocket exhaust when Surveyor 6 lifted off.

It has been revealed that surveyor 6 showed that spacecraft could land on the moon, and lift off again. Less than two years later, humans did the same thing during Apollo 11.

NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft rolled out to the moon on Nov. 7, 1967 and made its first landing on the lunar surface on Nov. 10 of that year. It's primary mission was to make a soft landing on the moon in the Sinus Medii of the moon.

Industry observers note that the probe took nearly 30,000 photos of the moon during its 16 days on the lunar surface, with the lander shutting down due to the onset of lunar night on Nov. 26. Surveyor 6 was the sixth and penultimate moon mission of NASA's Surveyor lunar program, so a lot of what it did (launching and landing on the moon) had been done before.

But a lunar liftoff? That was something new.

"On November 17, as an engineering test to see if its rockets could be restarted on the Moon, Surveyor’s engines fired for 2.5 seconds, lifting the spacecraft 12 feet high and moving it 8 feet west of its original landing site, in the first powered liftoff from another celestial body," NASA wrote in a mission overview.

The engineering test proved that a spacecraft could land on the moon, and then lift off and take flight once more. That capability was a core requirement for NASA's Apollo astronaut moon landings that followed, since astronauts needed a way to return home after visiting the moon.

But there was critical science Surveyor 6 was able to do with the lunar hop.

"This maneuver provided excellent views of the surface disturbances produced by the initial landing and the effects of firing rocket engines close to the lunar surface," scientists with the Lunar and Planetary Institute wrote in a summary. "Photography obtained after the hop contributed to the soil mechanics investigation.".

Surveyor 6 also had a bar magnet on its footpad that allowed scientists to test how magnetic the lunar regolith was at the landing site.

Civil Aviation Authority guidelines include the following warning: "If you use these devices where people can expect privacy, such as inside their home or garden, you're likely to be breaking data protection laws.".

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 2 min read (469 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • OPEC and its allies’ surprise move to slash oil production will soon be felt at US gas pumps.
  • The group known as OPEC+ unveiled Sunday it would cut oil production by more than 1.6 million barrels a day starting in May, running through the end of the year.
  • Sources indicate that the production cut announcement also had an immediate impact on gasoline futures, which will be passed onto US drivers much more quickly than the spike in oil prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OPEC and its allies’ surprise move to slash oil production will soon be felt at US gas pumps.

The group known as OPEC+ unveiled Sunday it would cut oil production by more than 1.6 million barrels a day starting in May, running through the end of the year. The news sent both Brent crude futures, the global oil benchmark, and WTI, the US benchmark, up about 6% in trading Monday.

Sources indicate that the production cut announcement also had an immediate impact on gasoline futures, which will be passed onto US drivers much more quickly than the spike in oil prices. RBOB, the most closely watched wholesale gasoline price, was up about 8 cents a gallon, or about 3%, in morning trading.

“I think OPEC is reawakening the inflation monster,” mentioned Tom Kloza, global head of energy analysis for OPIS, which tracks gas prices for AAA. “The White House has to be shocked and major-time pissed. It certainly alters the calculus for a while.”.

The national average for US gas prices stood at $3.51, on Monday, according to AAA. Kloza said he could see it getting up to $3.80 to $3.90 in relatively short order thanks to the move by OPEC.

In a recent development, “We’re not going to get back to $5 a gallon. I don’t think we’re even going as high as $4,” he said. But he said by the end of the summer US drivers could be back above year-earlier prices, especially if there is a hurricane or other storms affecting production along the Gulf Coast.

The average US regular gas price a year ago stood at $4.19 a gallon in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the disruption that caused to world’s energy markets. Prices eventually reached a record $5.02 a gallon on June 14, before starting a slow but steady decline over the course of more than three months during which the average price fell every day. The decline was partly driven by the release of oil from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, and partly by concerns that there could be a US or global recession that reduced the demand for gasoline.

Oil prices surge after OPEC+ producers announce surprise cuts.

Even at $3.51, US gas prices were just below the $3.53 average on Feb. 23, 2022, the day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

According to recent reports, kloza mentioned one thing keeping prices from getting anywhere near the record levels of 2022 is that the US plans additional releases from the SPR, and US oil production and refining capacity are both up. But a cut of 1 million barrels a day of oil by OPEC+ will not be easy to make up.

“They have ability to cut production and they seem motivated to do so,” he remarked.

ULA lost a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying 40 Amazon satellites 10 minutes after launch — but the failure began just after liftoff

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the failure of a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying a full load of internet satellites for Amazon was caused by an anomaly in its first-stage booster, rocket maker United Launch Alliance said today (Nov.
  • That failure — which led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites — was recognized about 10 minutes after liftoff, but the problems began much earlier than that, ULA said in a statement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the failure of a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying a full load of internet satellites for Amazon was caused by an anomaly in its first-stage booster, rocket maker United Launch Alliance said today (Nov. 17).

That failure — which led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites — was recognized about 10 minutes after liftoff, but the problems began much earlier than that, ULA said in a statement.

"While we appear to have lost telemetry and the mission at approximately 10 minutes into flight, early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance, resulting in stage separation occurring when the vehicle was low in altitude and below minimal velocity to reach orbit," ULA wrote in today's upgrade.

Industry observers note that the two-stage Vulcan Centaur is the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket, which will retire after just six more flights. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and now has a total of five launches under its belt.

The upcoming rocket has experienced problems on three of those missions. On both its second and fourth flights — which introduced in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — the nozzle of one of Vulcan's strap-on solid rocket boosters (SRBs) fell off about 30 seconds after liftoff.

It has been revealed that on both occasions, the rocket overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payloads to orbit. However, after the second occurrence, the U.S. Space Force paused national-security launches with Vulcan until ULA addressed the SRB nozzle matter. (The February 2026 flight was a Space Force mission.).

In a recent development, that work led to "design and process improvements to the nozzle," ULA mentioned in an Oct. 28 patch. And those tweaks apparently worked.

"All indications are that the solid rocket booster performance was nominal, following nozzle improvements implemented for this launch," the company wrote in today's update.

Vulcan's Centaur V upper stage, which features two RL-10C engines, did its job as well "but was unable to recover from the [booster] performance loss, resulting in loss of mission," ULA added.

Vulcan's first-stage booster is powered by two BE-4 engines, which are built by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin. Today's upgrade did not identify the exact problem with the booster; doing so will require more time, as the investigation has just begun.

If that investigation finds a serious issue with the BE-4, there could be broad ripple effects across the American space program. After all, that engine also powers the first stage of Blue Origin's Latest Glenn rocket, which is a key piece of hardware for NASA's Artemis program of moon exploration. (And New Glenn is presently recovering from a failure of its own — a massive explosion on the test stand that occurred on May 28.).

NASA prepares to integrate the Centaur V upper stage into its Space Launch System moon rocket, the vehicle that rolls out Artemis astronauts to space. So the fact that the Centaur performed nominally on Sunday is a bit of good news for the space agency.

Sources indicate that vulcan's grounding is a substantial deal, no matter what the anomaly investigation ends up finding. The U.S. doesn't have a surfeit of powerful rockets, after all, and two of them — Vulcan and New Glenn — are out of commission at the moment.

There's considerable pressure on both Vulcan and New Glenn to bounce back strong, for the nation faces an impending launch crunch in the next few years. SpaceX aims to retire its Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets and shift its launch load over to the fully reusable Starship megarocket. SpaceX is expected to prioritize its own needs in Starship's early days, using the vehicle primarily to build out its next-gen Starlink broadband constellation and Starmind AI data center network.

Sources indicate that the Vulcan failure also impacts Amazon — specifically, the firm's blueprint to build out Amazon Leo, which will compete with SpaceX's Starlink. Amazon has booked about 100 introduces on a variety of rockets to build its constellation, which will eventually consist of more than 3,200 satellites. Thirty-eight of those bookings are for Vulcan; Sunday's launch was the first of those.

The other rockets Amazon has booked are the Atlas V, Newly introduced Glenn, Falcon 9 and Arianespace's Ariane 6. About 400 operational Amazon Leo satellites have reached orbit to date across 14 launches (not including Sunday's failure).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for a lot of folks, Grand Theft Auto VI is an excuse to live out the life of a powerful criminal, or at least try to be the world's best virtual boyfriend. But for those of us who left the "rampaging through the streets in a tank" days behind us, it sounds like the game has a lot more to offer.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 seems to be defined as much by its embrace of the mundane as anything else. Early reviews and Rockstar's previews have highlighted some of the seemingly countless, completely boring activities in the game. There are plenty of clips making the rounds, too, and with AI making fake gameplay easier to pass off as the real thing, we can't verify every video out there. Still, I’ve seen enough to know what I’ll be doing while everyone else is on their crime sprees.

Industry observers note that one feature that some early GTA 6 launch coverage has highlighted is the ability for the protagonist Jason to fix up his house. This doesn't just have cosmetic benefits. Doing repairs can also earn Jason some goodwill with Lucia, his partner in crime and love interest.

According to recent reports, that means part of GTA 6's story will involve fixing a leaky roof, repairing a porch railing and stairs, and perhaps most excitingly, painting a bedroom wall. Yes, you can literally watch paint dry in GTA 6. This is what I've always wanted.

It has been revealed that developer Rockstar Games has become especially good at rendering the natural world in its more recent games, and it sounds like GTA 6 takes this to the next level. One major example of that is that you can devote your time to bird-watching, if you want.

Recent findings suggest that there are apparently 62 different kinds of birds in the game, and you can check them out with a pair of binoculars before recording them in a wildlife logbook. I'm not joking when I say I know at least one person in real life who will absolutely go through the effort of finding all 62 birds. Heck, I might do it, too.

Industry observers note that one of my favorite real-life pastimes is staring at my phone for way too much of every day. Constantly switching between and refreshing the same three social media apps is sorta like putting my brain in a microwave, and I just can't stop doing it.

According to recent reports, that's why I'm excited about the prospect of literally doing the same thing in GTA 6. You can sit in bed and just look at fake social media apps, which is genuinely probably a better and healthier use of time than looking at real ones.

Dogs are wonderful. I love dogs, and I'm glad that petting them has become an expected mechanic in so many video games in recent years. The fact that you can pet dogs in GTA 6 is old news at this point.

But I'm also a lifelong cat guy, and video games don't give cats nearly as much attention. Rockstar must have read my mind because you can totally pet cats in GTA 6.

You can bet your bottom dollar that I'll be doing that instead of robbing convenience stores.

It has been revealed that previous GTA games have given players the ability to watch things on TV. I'm old enough to remember watching Katt Williams do virtual stand-up in GTA 4, for example.

But GTA 6 steps that up by introducing an original cartoon series called Macca & Friends that you can apparently watch entirely in-game. That is stupid enough that I might actually do it.

Last but certainly not least, there is one optional side activity that every good video game ought to have: fishing. And guess what? You can totally fish in GTA 6.

It has been revealed that what else needs to be noted? Few things are more relaxing in real life and in virtual life than sitting back and doing some dang angling. I might crack open a cold one while doing this for maximum effect.
